pattern.top_pattern: Outpatient chemotherapy episodes are landing in Not Mapped buckets
pattern.what_is_impacting: OH / CA / TX / OP IV Thrpy/Oncology and OP Mgmt Oth Misc

providers: EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL

pattern.pattern_details: Outpatient chemotherapy-related episodes are repeatedly showing up in Not Mapped buckets across OH and CA, with a smaller related outpatient misc signal spanning CA and TX. The pattern is concentrated at GOOD SAMARITAN HOSPITAL, KETTERING HEALTH DAYTON, and EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL and appears tied to chemotherapy drug claims rather than a broad outpatient shift. This is a distinct authorization and mapping issue because oncology drug episodes may be classified outside the expected service line.
pattern.why_it_matters: Misclassified chemotherapy activity can distort oncology trend reporting, obscure authorization performance, and hide site-of-care opportunities.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Validate chemotherapy authorization records, drug coding, and service-line assignment for Z5111, Z5112, C180, and C679 episodes, and confirm whether these claims should be grouped under oncology rather than Not Mapped outpatient buckets.
pattern.validation_reason: Repeated oncology-related claims are landing in Not Mapped buckets, so service-line classification and authorization mapping may be distorting the pattern.
evidence_summary: OH outpatient oncology added about $118.0K at GOOD SAMARITAN HOSPITAL on 21 chemotherapy drug claims under Z5111.
OH outpatient misc chemotherapy added about $136.3K at KETTERING HEALTH DAYTON and GOOD SAMARITAN HOSPITAL under Z5112 and Z5111.
CA chemotherapy-related episodes added about $105.8K, led by EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL under C679 and C180.
Across these groups, chemotherapy is the dominant signal; smaller transport tails were only about $25.5K in OH and $13.0K in CA / TX.
